description: Phase 3 retrieval golden v1: ~10 hand-authored CI queries labeled against retrieval relevance-criteria policy v2. Authored from the SOURCE documents (data/reports/), never from extraction output. Golden spans are keyed (doc_id, line_range) at the finest answer-bearing resolution; line_range is the load-bearing key, verbatim is for human audit. This file is the fixed input the retrieval eval will score against once a retriever exists; it does NOT depend on or describe any retrieval implementation. Unlike the per-document extraction goldens (takeda/novartis.golden.json, which carry golden_schema_version), this is a query-based cross-document artifact with its own schema.

novartis.slice: partial: only chunks [3,4,12,13,15,16,18,28,29,30,31,32] of 100 are extracted; all other lines are un-extracted territory the entity leg cannot reach

policy_v2.1_answer_bearing: Judge relevance from source, never extraction output. A span is relevant only if read-alone it gives a direct, load-bearing component of the answer AND the fact's key is co-present with the value (for a pipeline/Program fact: asset + indication + the region/stage the query demands). A drug matched against the WRONG indication is NOT answer-bearing (validated at Q5: iptacopan-for-MG excluded from the IgAN answer). Excludes keyword-present non-answers: sales rows, positional-stage summary cells, bare-indication fragments.
policy_v2.2_containment: A retrieved unit HITS a golden span when >= T of the golden span's lines fall inside the unit (direction = how much of the answer the unit covers). T = 0.5 PROVISIONAL and explicitly DEFERRED — see t_calibration. answer-coverage-only; NOT the mashed-row false-credit detector (that is 5_resolution_limited).
policy_v2.3_construct_single: Single fact -> OR-of-locations: the relevant set is the union of source locations where the fact is independently answer-bearing; the fact HITS if any one location is retrieved (>=T). Per-fact spans on mashed rows each get their own golden span at finest answer-bearing resolution.
policy_v2.3_construct_set_of_singles_vs_aggregate: NEW (v2 clarification). The construct for a multi-fact query is decided by whether its relevant set is CLOSED or OPEN. (a) set-of-singles (bounded): relevant set is closed and knowable from the query itself — the query NAMES the specific entities/facts; each is an independent single (OR-of-locations) and ALL are required. Subtlety from Q1: a phrase like 'Multiple Indications' that is a literal SOURCE VALUE does NOT make a query an aggregate — what matters is whether the set is closed, not whether a word sounds categorical. (b) aggregate (open): relevant set is an open category the CORPUS defines — the query names a category, not a list ('the CV pipeline', 'all Phase 3 trials'); corpus determines membership/count; scored as recall-fraction over the row-set, graded, no importance bar. The test is closed-and-query-defined vs open-and-corpus-defined, NOT merely 'names specifics vs names a category'.
policy_v2.3_construct_comparison: Comparison query -> TWO coverage scores, never collapsed: presence_coverage = AND(entities compared) o OR(an entity's qualifying assets) o OR(locations) — does each side have a qualifying asset (company/entity grain is the headline; one-side-only scores 1/2). attribute_coverage = AND(qualifying assets) o OR(locations) — is the attribute captured for ALL qualifying assets. Both sliced extracted/un-extracted, keyed (doc_id, line_range). Two scores because one number lies when an entity has multiple assets at different attribute-values (Q5: Novartis = 3 IgAN assets at approved/filed/Phase 3).
policy_v2.3_construct_comparison_STATUS: KNOWN LIMITATION, not settled validation. The comparison construct has been exercised ONLY on its motivating case (Q5, IgAN). It is NOT yet validated on a fresh comparison instance, and in particular has NOT been tested against an entity with ZERO qualifying assets (where presence_coverage must score that side 0). To be re-evaluated, and revised if needed, on the first future comparison query that exposes a deficiency.
policy_v2.3_construct_aggregate_VALIDATION: VALIDATED on first new instance (Q4, CV pipeline): recall-over-row-set held; no new primitive needed. Caveat: the category boundary (denominator N) is a 1_answer_bearing labeling call (e.g. is PAH cardiovascular? is a marketed drug's new-indication row 'pipeline'?), not a representational failure of the recall construct.
policy_v2.4_conservative_miss: Borderline containment -> record the stricter outcome (MISS), tag borderline_containment. Never fudge toward HIT. Inert this pass (containment was bimodal 1.0/0.0 — see t_calibration).
policy_v2.5_resolution_limited: Fires when no answer-bearing span isolates the fact from its SIBLINGS, keyed to 1_answer_bearing. A 'sibling' (v2) is a COMPETING ANSWER TO THE SAME QUERY SLOT — only another fact that could answer the same query counts. A different-indication fact co-located in the same block is NOT a sibling and does NOT trigger the flag (Q1 Mult-Ind+AE, Q5 mezagitamab ITP+IgAN, Q7 VAY736 6-indication block all stay clean). SPAN-LEVEL not query-level: a fact may be resolution_limited in one location and clean in another; the golden links the locations so a retriever earns a clean HIT only by returning the isolating location. A resolution_limited HIT is reported in a separate slice, never silently upgraded to clean.
policy_v2.6_slice_and_keying: Every golden span keyed (doc_id, line_range) — line_range alone collides across documents. Each query/span tagged extracted vs un-extracted (entity leg structurally cannot reach un-extracted). Reporting ALWAYS sliced — never merge extracted and un-extracted into one coverage number.
policy_v2.7_out_of_scope: Unmodeled-entity content (deals/M&A) stays OUT of the retrieval golden and out of every recall denominator; may be cited in writeups as a schema-scope illustration only (Q2 Avidity).
policy_v2.t_calibration: T=0.5 is a DEFERRED DECISION with a stated trigger, not an oversight. Neither the two gates nor the labeling pass can falsify T: using extraction-provenance line_ranges as stand-in retrieved units biases containment to ~1.0 by construction (a fact's authored span sits inside the very chunk that extracted it), so containment is bimodal (1.0/0.0) and no span straddles a unit boundary. TRIGGER: calibrate T against the first real retrieval index, where sub-T containment can actually occur. Do not tune T from labeling.

validation_history.method: Two policy gates (Q3, Q5) labeled end-to-end to discover policy holes, then a full labeling pass with a tripwire on the first new relational query of each shape.
validation_history.gate_Q3: Resolution_limited gate. Broke v0 §5 (keyed on surface-token line-uniqueness; the mashed oveporexton main row defeated it) -> produced v2 §5 (sibling = competing same-slot answer; span-level).
validation_history.gate_Q5: Comparison gate. Broke v1 §3 (one-fact-one-span could not represent a multi-asset/multi-stage company) -> produced v2 §3 comparison (two coverage scores). Also caught a missed asset (Vanrafia).
validation_history.pass_tripwire: Tripwire on first new aggregate (Q4): §3 v2 aggregate construct HELD (recall-over-row-set; no new primitive). Tripwire stayed DRY. No new comparison appears in the seed set, so the comparison construct was NOT re-validated (see 3_construct_comparison_STATUS).
validation_history.inert_this_pass: §4 borderline_containment never fired (bimodal containment). §5 resolution_limited fired only at Q3; its v2 sibling-narrowing was exercised in the keep-clean direction (Q1, Q5, Q7) but not in the fire direction on any newly-labeled query.
